answer: Jittered handshake admission: each new identity must space its first 12 actions by delays drawn from a server seed and submit a client timing trace. If inter-arrival variance falls below threshold or matches another trace, it enters a 20-minute cooling queue capped at one action per minute. The seed is the kernel for delay checks. A mesa of queued identities gets no throughput. Saffron marks rechecked traces. An attacker pays 20 minutes plus one independent scheduler per identity; cloned schedules collapse into one bucket.
